This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **26** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `packages/spec/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **26** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `packages/spec/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 72 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **167** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c2e0c8571a319893ea5e65dc877e01ee5a58f828` — the merge of head `609a2715b06aac84ac1709d7b8144c8b92f010e9` into base `74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c2e0c8571a319893ea5e65dc877e01ee5a58f828 && git checkout c2e0c8571a319893ea5e65dc877e01ee5a58f828
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe 609a2715b06aac84ac1709d7b8144c8b92f010e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe && git merge --no-ff 609a2715b06aac84ac1709d7b8144c8b92f010e9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 74801d190f5f528712ae3ebd9e4cbef81d3f13fe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged against the head tree:

1. **`@objectstack/spec/data` and the root entry lose 11 value exports and 5 type exports** — `DataEngineRequestSchema`, its nine `DataEngine{Find,FindOne,Insert,Update,Delete,Count,Aggregate,Execute,VectorFind}RequestSchema` arms, `DataEngineContractSchema`; types `DataEngineRequest`, `DataEngineRequestParsed`, `DataEngineExecuteRequest`, `DataEngineInsertRequest`, `DataEngineVectorFindRequest`. **Right.** This is exactly the set the maintainer's ruling A (#27274, `6472013580`) retires, no more and no less. `api-surface/data.json`, `export-origins/data.json` and `declaration-map/data.json` shrink by the same names. A head-wide grep for the 16 names and the 5 private helpers (CHANGELOGs and `content/docs/releases/` excluded) finds only the retirement kit, the new pin, prose notes, `authorable-surface.base.json` (see 6) and the #4618 D3 entry's history sentence. `ui/` has zero hits; `skills/` has zero hits (so `Skills-docs: none` holds).
2. **The published JSON Schema loses 10 defs** (`data/DataEngineRequest` and the nine arm defs): `json-schema.manifest/data.json` −10, and each def is registered in `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR[18]` through one `retired-defs/18.data__*.ts` file whose filename and `entry` string agree under `shardNameFor` (`/` → `__`, `build-migration-registry.ts`). **Right**: the manifest deletion gate (#4725, `build-schemas.ts`) requires exactly this declaration, and the build passed with it.
3. **The authorable-surface ratchet loses 35 keys** over the nine arm defs (`authorable-surface/data.json`), `authorable-defaults/data.json` loses `data/DataEngineVectorFindRequest:limit = 5`. **Right**: the keys belonged to defs that no longer exist, the deletion is adjudicated by the retired-def registration, and the ledger row count moved under a `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` declaration, which is the only kind that may move it.
4. **Shrink-only ledgers shrink and never grow**: `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` −8 entries (252 → 244 schemas, 900 → 892 sites), `unemitted-schemas.baseline.json` −1 (`Data.DataEngineContractSchema`), `docs-import-surface.baseline.json` −6, `variant-docs.json` −1 (the `method:` union). **Right**; every move is a removal of a row about a retired def.
5. **No runtime accept set changes.** Nothing parsed the retired schemas (measured on the decision card and re-measured here: no parser or importer outside `packages/spec/src/data/`; the QuickJS sandbox speaks `ctx.api.object(name)`, `quickjs-runner.ts:17`; the wire batch validates with `CrossObjectBatchRequestSchema` / `BatchUpdateRequestSchema`, `rest/src/batch-routes.ts:243,442`). `RPC_QUERY_ALIAS_SLOTS`, `QUERY_TRANSPORT_ALIAS_SLOTS`, `foldQueryAliasSlots`, `aliasConflictIssue`, `QueryTransportParamsSchema`, `QueryWithTransportSchema` and every `*OptionsSchema` stay, and `QueryWithTransportSchema` still folds by the table (`data-engine.zod.ts:1025`). **Right**: the retirement removes a declaration, not a behaviour.
6. **`authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched and still carries the 35 rows.** **Right** by that file's own header: it is the deletion gate's pinned anchor at `baseRev`, "written only by `gen:schema`, only from a git-resolved baseline — never from the build that is being checked"; a PR that edited it to hide a deletion would go red. The #27182 precedent (`data/Document*`, 4 rows still in the anchor) followed the same path.
7. **`@objectstack/objectql`**: one comment moves (`engine.ts:600-601`, `RpcQueryOptionsSchema` → `QueryWithTransportSchema`). No surface change. **Right**: `QueryWithTransportSchema` is the schema that folds the four non-engine alias pairs at parse (`data-engine.zod.ts:1291-1299`).
8. **ADR-0087 chain**: one D3 semantic entry `data-engine-rpc-protocol-retired` in major 18 (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = '18.0.0'`, `protocol-version.ts:22`), no D2 conversion, no `retiredKey()` tombstone. **Right**: route 3 of `spec-property-retirement` as ruled; no metadata source authors these shapes (the keys were never under a `stack.zod.ts` key or a registered type) so a tombstone would prescribe through a parse that never runs. Same shape as `17.data-engine-batch-retired` and `18.document-schemas-retired`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27028-data-engine-rpc-protocol-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: patch`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; marker `adr-0087: registered data-engine-rpc-protocol-retired`; a BREAKING banner, a FROM → TO table covering all 16 names, and the one-line fix (TS2305 after upgrade). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines.
- **Level matches what the diff publishes.** Under ruling A of 2026-10-21 (mechanized in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "The LEVEL axis"), the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone: `narrowed` requires at least one moved package at `minor` or above (spec, `minor`: met); `major` is refused in the launch window and ADR-0087 lets the pre-GA break land one-step as a chain step (the D3 entry: present). `objectql` `patch` is right for a comment-only edit in a published package. `authorable-surface/` and `authorable-defaults/` shards moved, which rules out `none`; `narrowed` is the kind for a key removed. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are green on this head.
- **`Clause-②:` line.** `no (narrowing)` is the spelling this review's own face is cut on (the record shape names it as the narrowing face) and the one the gates read: the `(narrowing)` arm is the ADR-0087 breaking signal (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:718`), and `narrowed` beside a line without that arm is a contradiction the level gate refuses. The spelling is the repo's established one for an accept-set or export narrowing (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:88,143,162,9945`; pending `.changeset/26954-engine-projection-empty.md`). The decision card's draft wrote `yes (narrowing)`; the claim, the director's workload line and the PR all wrote `no (narrowing)`. The arm, not the yes/no, is what every reader consumes, so the discrepancy is immaterial to the verdict; noted for the record.
- `skip-changeset` is not involved. The `feat(spec)!:` title carries the breaking marker. **PASS on ②.**

No local re-run is owed.
2. **`IDataEngine` doc comments still say "remote/virtual engines" as hypothetical implementers that may omit optional members.** Answered: lines 354, 369, 404, 516 of `contracts/data-engine.ts` are about optional-member TypeScript posture, not the retired wire protocol, and may stand. **But** lines 172-173 of the same file still read "nothing here crosses the RPC / Virtual Data Engine boundary" — the exact phrase this PR rewrote at line 61. That is a stale reference to the retired protocol inside a `hits` file; see ④.1 (should-fix).

4. **Tier.** The seat's 席位核对 (`6475302405`, head `644adb1e7`) found `check-governed-merges --pr 27324` NOT governed and ACCEPTed at Tier S. That reading predates `1a50dca1e`, which edits `docs/adr/0119-...md`. `docs/adr/**` is a `GOVERNED_TIER_H` register row (`check-governed-merges.mjs:1201`), and one Tier H path makes the whole PR Tier H (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14). The PR body says so (“请审批并合并（Tier H）”). **Escalated**: landing on this head is the maintainer's hand or an authorized APPROVED review; the seat's Tier S ACCEPT is stale on this head and must not arm the queue. This record is the contract-tier review the Tier H landing also wants; it does not substitute for the maintainer's approval. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green (it guards the queue, not the landing).

The ratchet test passed, so nothing is red; a one-clause note on that row would keep the ledger's prose honest. Lane remainder, should-fix at most.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file, judged against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against (ruling A on #27274; the published spec on `main`; its first consumer).

1. **`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`** (comment-only, line 61). Holds: `WriteObservabilityOptions` is a TS-contract-only bag; "a function is unrepresentable in JSON Schema and cannot be serialized, so remote callers (REST, the client SDK) simply never receive these events" is true of the tree (the serializable bags are `Engine*OptionsSchema`; REST and the client SDK are the remote callers that exist). Tried to break it: searched the file for every other naming of the retired boundary. **Should-fix:** lines 172-173 (`strictReadonlyWrites` docblock, "In-process only — what a REMOTE caller observes") still say "crosses the RPC / Virtual Data Engine boundary or is reachable from a REST/wire body". With the protocol retired in this same PR there is no RPC / Virtual Data Engine boundary in the spec to cross; the sentence should read as line 61 now does ("cannot be serialized … REST/wire body"). Same class as the edit the PR made, one occurrence missed; no behaviour, no export, no gate touched. Not a must-fix.
2. **`packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts`.** The deletion is exactly the ruled set; every surviving neighbour the arms depended on is still consumed (`aliasConflictIssue` and `foldQueryAliasSlots` by `QueryWithTransportSchema`, `transportProjectionArray` by `DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema.select`:219 and the transport dialect, `FilterConditionSchema` by the filter schemas). The section-8 note's claims about `DataEngineContractSchema` hold against the deleted code and the contract: its `find`/`findOne`/`count` inputs were `[string, Options?]` with no trailing `options?: BaseEngineOptions` (`IDataEngine.find`:301, `count`:322), it declared neither `vectorFind?` (:328) nor `execute?` (:343), and it never emitted (`unemitted-schemas.baseline.json`, cause `function`). The section-9 note names the doors that exist, each verified: QuickJS sandbox `ctx.api.object(name)` (`quickjs-runner.ts:17`), wire batch via `CrossObjectBatchRequestSchema` / `BatchUpdateRequestSchema` (`batch-routes.ts:243,442`). The #26954 projection comment is corrected to the two engine-side declarations that remain. The `RPC_QUERY_ALIAS_SLOTS` docblock now points at `QueryWithTransportSchema` and `QUERY_TRANSPORT_ALIAS_SLOTS` (:750, which extends the table with `filters` / `$filter` / `$expand`): true. The word "RPC" survives only in the table's name and its two-line description, which the ruling kept by name. Tried to break it: does anything author these shapes (stack key, registered type, Studio form, CLI)? No — the keys were in the authorable ratchet only because the schema was published, not because any carrier reached them; so route 3 (no tombstone) is the right route and a `retiredKey()` here would be unreachable noise. No finding.
3. **The ten `retired-defs/18.data__DataEngine*Request.ts` files.** Filename ↔ `entry` string agree under `shardNameFor`; major 18 is the current protocol major; each def is one the manifest on `main` published and this diff removes (ten manifest lines removed, ten entries added; `data/DataEngineRequest` plus nine arms, none missing, none extra). The header note states the ruling, the measurement trees and the route. First consumer (`build-schemas.ts` manifest deletion gate, #4725) accepted them: build green. No finding.
4. **`semantic/18.data-engine-rpc-protocol-retired.ts`.** Conforms to `SemanticMigration` (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; `conversionIds` and `relevantWhen` omitted, as in the two precedents and as `types.ts` prescribes for a surface not under stack keys). `surface` carries no backticks and no pipe, which `build-upgrade-guide.ts:135` needs (it renders `surface` inside a code span). `replacement` names only doors that exist: `IDataEngine` at `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (`package.json` exports `./contracts`), `ctx.api.object(name).find(...)`, REST `/data/:object` and `POST /data/:object/query` (`metadata-protocol/protocol.ts:4884`), `POST {basePath}/batch` with the two batch schemas; "`DataEngineContractSchema` has no replacement schema: the engine contract is the `IDataEngine` interface" is true. `acceptanceCriteria` is checkable and is checked (the new pin asserts TS2305 is named, the defs are absent from the manifest, and the lit controls survive). **Should-fix (prose precision, not a prescription change):** `reason` says "every arm admitted a caller-supplied `context` (`isSystem` included)". Against the deleted code, seven of the nine arms did (their `query` / `options` bags extend `BaseEngineOptionsSchema`, whose `context: ExecutionContextSchema.partial().optional()`, :76); `execute` carried an untyped `options` record and `vectorFind` carried `vector` / `where` / `fields` / `limit` / `threshold` and no `context` at all. The decision card's wording ("every read and write arm") was exact; the entry and the changeset generalize it to "every arm". The judgment the upgrader owes does not change, so this is a should-fix in a load-bearing prose field, not a must-fix.
5. **`packages/spec/src/ui/view-grouping-query.ts`** (comment-only). "in process the same body is `IDataEngine.aggregate`'s `EngineAggregateOptions`" holds: `aggregate(objectName: string, query: EngineAggregateOptions, options?: BaseEngineOptions)` (`contracts/data-engine.ts:323`). The route it still names (`client.data.query()` → the `hasGroupBy || hasAggregations` branch) is unchanged by this PR. No finding.
6. **`docs/adr/0119-plugin-reachable-transactions-and-honest-atomic-batch.md`.** The edit replaces one `path#DataEngineRequest` symbol anchor, which this PR makes unresolvable, with a file-level anchor on `packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` (the `[unresolved-symbol]` remedy `check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` itself prescribes when the symbol is gone), and adds a dated editorial note in the ADR's own 2026-08-05 style, naming the registering entry by path (a second file-level anchor, resolving). The decision (D3: `batch?` retired) is unchanged, and its first consumer agrees: `contracts/data-engine.ts:330-338` records `batch?` as retired under ADR-0119 D3 and points at the same three replacements the D3 entry and the kernel docs page now name (`IObjectQLEngine.transaction`, `objectql-engine.ts:533`; `batchData` `options.atomic`, `protocol.ts:14577`; `POST {basePath}/batch`).
